Order
Regard being had to the similitude in the controversy involved in these criminal revisions, therefore,
these criminal revisions were analogously heard and are being disposed off by this common order.

2. Both the revision petitions arises from the order dated 18.01.2019 in ST No.100627/2016 arising out of Crime No.200/02 registered at Police NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3438 2 CRR-1622-2019 Station Bhikamgaon, District Mandleshwar by the Additional Session Judge,
Bhikamgaon, M.P. whereby charges under Section 420, 467, 468, 471 of the IPC, 1860 and Section 39 r/w 192 and Section 66 r/w 192 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 have been framed against Bhgwati Bai (revision petitioner in CRR No.1547/2019) & Gopal (revision petitioner in CRR No.1622/2019)
and charges under Section 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the IPC have been framed against Anil (revision petitioner No.1 in criminal revision No.1547/2019).
3. The prosecution case, as projected before the trial Court is that on 18.06.2002 bus Vehicle No.MP-09-S-7847, MP-09-S-3147 belonging to Balaji travels were inspected by Police Station - Bhikangaon.
The documents including permit were not available with the bus.

After sometime, one accused Ghanshyam Rathore reached at the spot and submitted the Xerox copy of the permits and Anil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49458052/
1 R.C. books of the vehicles and submitted that due to safety reasons, the original documents are kept safe with the office.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the inconvenience of the passenger in the vehicle buss were permitted to move further and the photocopies that were provided were forwarded to the transport office for verification.
After verification, it was found that vehicles are being plied on the basis of forged permits.

Initially, the final report was submitted against Uday, Suneel, Santosh,
Shyamkumar, Kamal, Ghanshyam keeping the investigation pending, for the rest of persons.
Thereafter, completing the investigation, the supplementary charge- sheet was submitted against Bhagwati Bai w/o Ghanshyam Rathore, Santosh S/o Radheshyam and Anil S/o Laxman Rathore.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3438 3 CRR-1622-2019 4.
Matter was committed to the Session's court and charges were framed.

5. Challenging the framing of charges, the revision petitioner in Criminal Revision No.1547/2019 has challenged the framing of charges on the ground that the essential ingredients of the offence are lacking on the basis of material collected during investigation.
The trial Court proceeded on the basis of unwarranted inferences.

6. Criminal Revision No.1622/2019 is preferred on the ground that the letter dated 10.07.2002 (Annexure-A/1) issued by the office of Deputy Collector, Indore, addressed to the office of Station House Officer, Bhikangaon, District Khargone has reported that the permit in respect of vehicle No.MP-09-S-3147 is regular and correct and there is no illegality with it.
The statement of Manish Singh (Annexure-A/2) recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C. also confirmed that there is no illegality in the permit of the present petitioner.
The forged permit relating to the Vehicle No.MP-09-S-7847 and Vehicle No.MP-09-S-3147 were submitted by one Ghanshyam and not by the present petitioner.
The present petitioner Gopal Rathore was having a valid permit.
The charges have been framed in cyclostyle manner.
They are similar in respect of all persons.
The charges have been framed with an inordinate delay of 17 years.
His fundamental right to the speedy trial has been infringed.

In support of his petition he placed reliance on various cases i.e. Maneka Gandhi vs.
Union of India; AIR 1978 SC 597, Hussainhara Khatoon vs. State of Bihar; AIR 1979 SC 1360, State of Maharashtra vs. Champalal Panajee Shah; AIR 1981 SC 1675, T.V.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3438 4 CRR-1622-2019 Vatheeswaran vs. State of Tamilnadu; AIR 1983 SC 361, State of Bihar vs. Uma Shankar Kotniwal; AIR 1981 SC 641, S. Guin vs. Grindlays Bank Ltd. AIR 1986 SC 289, State of Bihar vs. Maksudan Singh; AIR 1986 Pat 38 and Madheshwardhari Singh vs. State of Bihar; AIR 1986; 1986 Cri LJ 1771 (FB).

7. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the revision petitions.

8. The report of the State Examiner of Questioned Documents, Government of Madhya Pradesh,
dated 16.09.2003

, states that the standard seal impression, stamped and marked as S1, does not tally in size, design, or the relative placement of letters with the red-enclosed questioned seal Anil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49458052/
2 impressions stamped and marked as Q1 to Q5.

entities.text: Anil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The questioned seal impression marked Q2 is affixed on the temporary permit purportedly issued by the Regional Transport Officer, Indore, for bus bearing registration No. MP-09-S-3147, valid for the period from 01.06.2002 to 30.06.2002, for operation on various routes originating from Khandwa.
9. Accordingly, the pleas raised on behalf of the revision petitioner, Gopal, pertain to the matter of defence and are required to be considered at the appropriate stage of trial.

Considering the nature of the offence, the revision petitioner Gopal is not entitled to discharge merely by placing reliance on the decisions in Maneka Gandhi (supra), Hussainhara Khatoon (supra), Champalal Panajee Shah (supra), T.V. Vatheeswaran (supra), Uma Shankar Kotniwal (supra), S. Guin (supra), Maksudan Singh (supra) and Madheshwardhari Singh (supra) on the ground of delay, as the so called NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3438 5 CRR-1622-2019 delay is attributable to the revision petitioner also for consuming a significant period by challenging the proceedings of the trial Court.
Consequently, Criminal Revision No. 1622/2019 filed by the revision petitioner Gopal fails and is hereby dismissed.
Now, come to the Criminal Revision No.1547/2019 filed on behalf of Anil and Bhagwatibai.
10. The report of the Collector and District Magistrate, Indore, dated 10.07.2002, provides sufficient material for framing of charges against the revision petitioners Anil and Bhagwatibai Rathore.
Any error in reference to the bus number may be rectified by the Trial Court, and such an error does not constitute a ground for discharge.
11. Similarly, revision petitioner Anil was working with Balaji Travels and had obtained custody of all the vehicles on supurdgi.
There is sufficient material on record against the revision petitioners to proceed with the matter.
Accordingly, Criminal Revision No. 1547/2019 filed by the revision petitioners Anil and Bhagwatibai Rathore lacks merit and is hereby dismissed.

12. Let a copy of this order be placed in connected matter and the record of the trial Court be remitted back immediately.
(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE VS Anil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49458052/
